title: They didn’t just get the Ten Commandments once.
paragraphs: They didn’t just get the Ten Commandments once.
And most people miss why that matters.
The first time, in Exodus 20, God Himself writes the law on stone—holy, pure, untouched.
But before Moses even comes down the mountain…
Israel is already dancing around a golden calf.
Not out of rage alone—but as a visible sign:
The covenant was broken before it even reached the people.
In Exodus 34, the commandments are given again.
“The Lord, the Lord, compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abounding in love…” (Exodus 34:6)
Then later, in Deuteronomy 5, Moses repeats the commandments again—but now with explanation, with context, with relationship.
“You were slaves… and the Lord brought you out.”
Here’s the truth most people miss:
The Ten Commandments were never just about rules.
And with a reminder of redemption.
And that’s where grace walks in.
Because the Law was written on stone…
But Jesus came to write it on hearts.
Through Jeremiah 31:33, God promised a new covenant.
You don’t stand before God based on how perfectly you kept the commandments.
You stand by the One who fulfilled them.
Jesus Christ didn’t come to erase the law—
And then carry your failure on the cross.
So if you feel like you’ve already “broken the tablets” of your life…
Now you’re exactly where grace begins.
